description: It is not established whether the CBCG publishes drafts of its own secondary legislation (nacrti odluka) for public comment, or adopts them at Savjet sessions without prior consultation. Only ministry-run consultations on primary laws were confirmed.

No page publishing supervisory enforcement actions, sanctions, fines, or mjere prema kreditnim institucijama was located. Only the 'restriktivne mjere' (international sanctions lists) node and the 'oduzeto odobrenje' payments list were observed, which are different things.

The cell scope names supervisory circulars, but no distinct circular/instruction channel (okruznice, uputstva, misljenja, cesto postavljana pitanja for supervised entities) was identified as separate from the formal Odluke corpus.

Montenegro's banking/payments regulatory agenda is driven largely by EU accession Chapters 4 and 9. EU-side documents (European Commission Montenegro country report, screening and negotiating-chapter material, ECB/EBA convergence and technical-cooperation outputs) were not scouted in this pass and sit outside cbcg.me.
No mechanism was identified for retrieving superseded versions of CBCG Odluke; the site appears to present only the current corpus, and no CBCG-side archive node was observed.

Searching used Montenegrin/Serbian latinica only. Cyrillic variants and a small number of ijekavica/ekavica spelling differences (sprjecavanje vs sprecavanje, izvjestaj vs izvestaj) were not systematically exercised, and diacritics were dropped in some queries.

No structured/machine-readable interface (API, OAI/RSS, open-data dataset) was confirmed for either zakoni.skupstina.me or the Official Gazette. Collection would currently rest on HTML scraping and PDF harvesting.

The practical fallback for consolidated texts and gazette contents (me.propisi.net, katalogpropisa.me) is commercial. Terms of service and whether systematic retrieval is permitted were not established.

Within the law-making pipeline, several actors were identified by name but not yet resolved to a monitored URL: Sekretarijat za zakonodavstvo (legal-technical vetting and prečišćeni tekstovi), Zaštitnik/Ustavni sud (constitutional challenges to financial statutes, one such 2026 decision was referenced), and the Fiskalni savjet established in 2026.

No Montenegrin crypto-asset / MiCA-alignment bill was found in the pipeline; press reporting explicitly states Montenegro still lacks a crypto-asset law and EU alignment is pending. Similarly, no dedicated instant-payments or open-banking bill was identified separately from the Zakon o platnom prometu amendments.

English-language coverage of this cell is thin and derivative. Parliament offers an English entry point (zakoni.skupstina.me/25saziv/index.php/en/) and gov.me publishes some /en/ articles, but bill texts, consultation notices, gazette issues and transposition tables are Montenegrin-only.

Bills adopted by skraćeni or hitni postupak bypass or compress public consultation, so the Ministry of Finance javna rasprava feed will not see them at all — they surface only at the Vlada session or directly on the parliamentary agenda.

Italian and Austrian parent groups with Montenegrin or adjacent exposure (Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit, Erste Group, Addiko, Sparkasse) were not individually source-mapped in this pass beyond the SSM/SRB umbrella and the Addiko takeover thread.
No Albanian- or Macedonian-language sources were covered, although North Macedonia and Albania joined SEPA on the same track as Montenegro and share the same EU alignment timetable.
Official gazettes as primary legal-effect sources were only reached indirectly (via Paragraf and HNB references to Narodne novine / Službeni glasnik).
Consultation/public-hearing mechanics for the regional regulators (how and where 'javna rasprava' drafts are posted, and with what comment deadlines) were not resolved to specific landing pages.

Regional card-scheme, ATM/POS-acquiring and payment-infrastructure operators (regional processors, ACH/instant-payment operators such as Serbia's IPS, Croatia's NKS) were not covered as spillover sources.
Domestic banking-ranked firms (Prelevic, Harrisons, Radonjic/Associates, Vukotic/Kaludjerovic-type boutiques, JPM Montenegro) lack confirmed publication URLs.
Montenegrin advisers appear to distribute client alerts via LinkedIn posts and PDF attachments rather than website blogs, a channel this run could not sample.
PwC Montenegro and EY Montenegro alert channels were not located; only KPMG ME and Deloitte ME alert archives were identified.
Non-legal advisory commentary (bank association, compliance consultancies, AML training providers, chambers of commerce guidance to members) was not covered in this cell's run.
Little evidence was found of advisory commentary on drafts at the public-consultation stage (javna rasprava) as opposed to adopted laws.

No broadcast/audio-visual monitoring: TV debate shows and radio interviews (RTCG, Vijesti TV, Antena M, Prva TV) are where governors, ministers and bank-association heads make unscripted statements about supervisory action and draft laws, and these are not captured by text crawling.
Albanian-language Montenegrin media (serving the Ulcinj/Tuzi communities) were not searched at all in this slice, despite the run scope naming sr and en only.

The cell's payments half is thin: searches surfaced banking supervision and AML richly, but almost nothing on media scrutiny of payment institutions, e-money issuers, card schemes or the instant-payments rollout beyond a single implementation-date item.

Montenegrin portals rewrite URLs and remove or paywall older items; several key outlets (Vijesti, Pobjeda, intellinews) have partial paywalls, so historical enforcement coverage may not be retrievable later.
Three candidates (dan.co.me, monitor.co.me, and the SeeNews hypothesis) rest on background knowledge of the Montenegrin press rather than on a search result returned in this run.
No per-bank career-page registry exists yet for the 11 licensed Montenegrin banks.
Vacancy adverts are published in the daily newspaper 'Dan' on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Any advert that is print-only would be invisible to a web collector.
There is no consolidated calendar of Montenegrin banking/payments events; agendas surface piecemeal via bankar.me, CBCG news and organiser sites, often only after the event.
The two richest specialist-role surfaces (LinkedIn job search, Facebook vacancy groups) are auth-walled and their terms prohibit automated collection.

Montenegrin FIU and Ministarstvo finansija training/vacancy activity is not yet resolved to specific pages, and university programmes (e.g. Ekonomski fakultet UCG) were not searched for payments/compliance specialisations.

No court/insolvency register was identified: no searchable bankruptcy (stečaj) or liquidation register for Montenegrin companies, and no public case-law/decision database for the commercial court (Privredni sud) was located.
No proactive archiving of Montenegrin regulator pages is in place; Wayback coverage depth for cbcg.me register pages and euprava.gov.me consultation pages is unknown.

Coverage is strong in Montenegrin/Serbian Latin script but nothing was tested in Cyrillic script variants (e.g. 'Регистар банака', 'Службени лист Црне Горе'), and no check was made for whether official sites serve Cyrillic mirrors.

Foreign/EU institutions operating into Montenegro (representative offices of foreign banks, cross-border card acquirers, crypto-asset service providers under any new ME regime) have no identified register.
Whether the beneficial-ownership register and CRPS permit systematic (as opposed to case-by-case) lookups is unresolved; both may impose digital-certificate authentication or fees for full extracts.
Fitch Ratings coverage of Montenegro was not confirmed in this pass; only Moody's (Ba3, positive) and S&P were evidenced. Whether Fitch maintains a Montenegro sovereign rating is unresolved.
The IMF/World Bank FSAP evidence found is dated (2015-2016 cycle plus 2019 report). Whether a newer Montenegro FSAP has been scheduled or delivered was not established.
Local-language (sr/Montenegrin) discovery in this cell was productive for MONEYVAL/AML and IMF terms but shallow for supervisory-cooperation, SEPA/payment-scheme and EU-acquis-chapter terminology.

No structured deadline/commitment tracker was identified. Assessor deadlines are currently scattered across MONEYVAL follow-up cycles, EC annual reports and IMF Article IV commitments with no single machine-readable calendar.

Council of Europe / EU joint technical-assistance projects in Montenegro (e.g. the AML capacity-building programmes referenced by EEAS and the Rule of Law Platform) were noted but not mapped as sources.

No source located for a securities/investor-compensation fund, a deposit protection body outside CBCG scope, or the Central Depository Agency (CDA/Centralna klirinško depozitarna društva) whose rulebooks bind banks acting as custodians — the T+1 settlement change from 1 January 2027 implies such rulebooks exist.
None of the cell's regulators (FIU, KTK, AZLP, ANO, UIP) were confirmed to offer RSS, an API, or an open-data export. All appear to require HTML scraping and PDF harvesting.

Consultation and in-force deadlines are expressed in prose inside Montenegrin-language PDFs and news items ('javna rasprava traje 24 dana', 'od 1. januara 2027'), not in structured fields anywhere in this cell.

English coverage of these non-central-bank bodies is very thin: only the Capital Market Authority and MONEYVAL offered substantive English pages. AZLP, the FIU and the inspectorate are effectively Montenegrin-only.

Inspection findings and sanctions imposed on banks and payment firms by these non-CBCG bodies were not located in any consolidated form; AZLP publishes individual rješenja and UIP publishes aggregate annual reports, but there is no per-entity enforcement register.

The Skupština Crne Gore (Parliament) pipeline — bill tabling, committee stage, adopted texts — was not sourced in this pass, though a Predlog zakona o tržištu kapitala PDF surfaced indirectly via a commercial aggregator.
The Ministry of Finance's own EU-alignment/negotiation pages and its document register were not directly located, only reached via gov.me article pages.
Montenegro's Reform Agenda document itself (the Growth Plan country annex with dated financial/payments steps) was not retrieved — only programme-level pages and disbursement news.
Non-bank supervisory bodies named as twinning beneficiaries — notably the Insurance Supervision Agency and the capital-markets supervisor — were not indexed as sources in this cell.
No parliamentary-committee channel indexed: the Odbor za evropske integracije of the Skupština, which reviews negotiating positions and alignment reports, was not resolved to a live page.
PSD3/PSR, AMLR/AMLA and DORA-equivalent alignment intentions for Montenegro were not evidenced by any specific document found in this pass; only PSD2 alignment of the payments law was confirmed.
All URLs in this slice were derived from search-result metadata and snippets; none were confirmed reachable by this agent.

The identity and publication channel of Montenegro's NASO (National Adherence Support Organisation) for SEPA scheme adherence is unconfirmed — likely CBCG or Udruženje banaka Crne Gore, but not verified.
The instant-payment scheme rulebook, technical specifications and participant list for the Montenegrin TIPS Clone were not retrieved (the hosting CBCG page failed to fetch once).
No official gazette (Službeni list Crne Gore) endpoint was captured directly; gazette references reached me only second-hand through CBCG and media.
Card-scheme and switch coverage is thin and vendor-mediated; no acquirer/issuer processing map or interchange regulation source was established.

Instant payments, RTGS/DNS and SEPA were searched thoroughly in Serbian/Montenegrin, but the QR-standard and card-scheme sub-topics lacked verified local terminology, weakening local-language recall there.

Reported compliance clocks (8 days for basic rules, 9 months for verification of payee, 18 months for batch verification, EUR 1,000 cap, 10-second availability) come from press reporting rather than from the legal text.
Four of the seven licensed payment institutions have no identified public channel (site, blog, news feed) for compliance or product announcements.
Operator terms-of-service and tariff documents were confirmed for only Presto Pay and CKB; the systematic 'opšti uslovi poslovanja' / 'tarifnik' layer across all ME PSPs is not yet enumerated.
Card acquiring, POS and e-commerce gateway providers serving ME merchants are unmapped.
The per-institution registration PDFs linked from the CBCG payment-institution register were not individually retrieved in this pass, so exact licence scopes, dates and agent lists are not captured.
No operator-facing public consultation channel specific to payments regulation was identified in this cell (e.g. draft decisions open for PSP comment).
Four licensed banks (Universal Capital Bank, Zapad banka, Ziraat Bank Montenegro, Adriatic Bank) were enumerated from the CBCG directory but their disclosure/terms sections were not located this run.

No bank was found publishing a standalone compliance/regulatory statement (e.g. AML, sanctions, DORA/PSD2-equivalent readiness, ESG/CSRD compliance) as a distinct document, beyond privacy notices and codes of conduct.
English-language mirrors exist for at least NLB (/en/) and several banks, but no systematic check was made of whether EN mirrors carry the same notices as the SR pages.

Historical versions of general terms and fee tariffs are typically overwritten; banks publish only the currently applicable version, so the change history that evidences notice periods is not natively retrievable.
This cell was scoped to banks; payment institutions, e-money institutions and MFIs licensed by CBCG have parallel notice/disclosure duties and were not covered.
No association representing non-bank payment service providers, e-money institutions, fintechs, leasing or microfinance companies was identified for Montenegro.
Association consultation responses (primjedbe na nacrt zakona) are not systematically primary-published; only fragments reached via press were observed.
komora.me association-board and legislation slugs could not be resolved live (404s on indexed URLs).
Coverage was built with Montenegrin/Serbian (ijekavian) terms only; no check was made for Cyrillic-script or Albanian-language variants of association names.
Consumer-protection associations, which routinely respond to banking and payments consultations elsewhere in the region, were not scouted in this pass.
No RSS/Atom feed was observed on UBCG, and feed availability was not established for komora.me, poslodavci.org, mfic.me or nbocg.me.

Financial-sector contracting authorities beyond CBCG and Ministarstvo finansija were not individually mapped in this pass: Agencija za nadzor osiguranja (insurance supervisor), Komisija za tržište kapitala, Fond za zaštitu depozita, Poreska uprava / Uprava prihoda i carina, Investiciono-razvojni fond (IRF), and the Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca.
No confirmed structured/bulk access route to CeJN notices (API, OpenData, RSS, or bulk XML) was identified.

Bilateral donors and other IFIs active in Western Balkan financial-sector reform were not covered: KfW/GIZ, IFC, IMF technical assistance, Council of Europe Development Bank, USAID successor programmes, and the Western Balkans Investment Framework (WBIF) project pipeline.

The pointer function of this cell — identifying bidders and awardees in Montenegrin financial-sector IT — was only established structurally (award notices exist, awardee names published) but no actual vendor names were harvested.
No archival source for pre-CeJN (pre-2018/2020) Montenegrin procurement notices was identified; the previous portal under Uprava za javne nabavke may no longer be live.
Search used Montenegrin/Serbian (Latin) only; Cyrillic-script variants and Albanian-language channels (relevant for some municipal/ethnic-minority-area publications) were not tried.
Core banking system attribution is unmapped for most of the 11 licensed banks; only digital-channel and ATM/POS suppliers are traceable.

Recruitment and tender-adjacent sources (bank career pages, Montenegrin job boards, vendor local job ads) were not searched in this pass but are a first-principles high-yield route to technology stack disclosure.
Scheme partner directories (Visa Ready, Mastercard Engage) were identified as pointer sources but their Montenegro-level filtering and ToS position were not verified.
Foreign-owned banks (OTP/CKB, NLB, Erste, Addiko, Ziraat) may take technology decisions at group level, so the Montenegro-specific supplier trace is systematically incomplete.
No Montenegrin ATM/POS hardware reseller or maintenance provider besides Payten was identified; competitor presence (e.g. other regional service providers) is unmapped.
